title: KCET 2021 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: In Chrysoberyl, a compound containing Beryllium, Aluminium and oxygen, oxide ions form cubic close packed structure. Aluminium ions occupy 1/4th of tetrahedral voids and Beryllium ions occupy 1/4th of octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: For n oxide ions (ccp), tetrahedral voids = 2n and octahedral voids = n. Al at 1/4 of 2n = n/2, Be at 1/4 of n = n/4. Ratio Be:Al:O = 1/4:1/2:1 = 1:2:4, giving BeAl$_2$O$_4$.

questions.q: The correct statement regarding defects in solids is
options: Frenkel defect is a vacancy defect
Schottky defect is a dislocation defect
Trapping of an electron in the lattices leads to the formation of F-centre
Schottky defect has no effect on density.
questions.explanation: An electron trapped in an anion vacancy of the crystal lattice is called an F-centre (Farbe centre); the other statements describe Frenkel/Schottky defects incorrectly.

questions.q: A metal crystallises in BCC lattice with unit cell edge length of 300 pm and density 6.15 g cm$^{-3}$. The molar mass of the metal is

Henry's law constant for the solubility of N$_2$ gas in water at 298 K is 1.0 × 10$^5$ atm. The mole fraction of N$_2$ in air is 0.8. The number of moles of N$_2$ from air dissolved in 10 moles of water at 298 K and 5 atm pressure is
questions.explanation: Partial pressure of N$_2$ = 0.8 × 5 = 4 atm. Mole fraction dissolved, x = p/K$_H$ = 4/10$^5$ = 4×10$^{-5}$. Moles of N$_2$ ≈ x × 10 (moles of water) = 4.0 × 10$^{-4}$.

questions.q: A pure compound contains 2.4 g of C, 1.2 × 10$^{23}$ atoms of H, 0.2 moles of oxygen atoms. Its empirical formula is
Choose the correct statement
options: K$_H$ value is same for a gas in any solvent
Higher the K$_H$ value more the solubility of gas
K$_H$ value increases on increasing the temperature of the solution
Easily liquefiable gases usually has lesser K$_H$ values
questions.explanation: Since solubility of a gas decreases with rise in temperature, the Henry's law constant K$_H$ increases with increase in temperature.

questions.q: The K$_H$ value (K bar) of Argon (I), Carbondioxide (II) formuldehyde (III) and methane (IV) are respectively 40.3, 1.67, 1.83 × 10$^{-5}$ and 0.413 at 298 K. The increasing order of solubility of gas in liquid is
questions.explanation: Solubility is inversely proportional to K$_H$. Decreasing K$_H$ order: I(40.3) > II(1.67) > IV(0.413) > III(1.83×10$^{-5}$), so increasing solubility order is I < II < IV < III.

questions.q: The vapour pressure of pure liquids A and B are 450 and 700 mm of Hg at 350 K respectively. If the total vapour pressure of the mixture is 600 mm of Hg, the composition of the solution in the mixture is

Consider the following electrodes: P = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.0001 M)/Zn, Q = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.1 M)/Zn, R = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.01 M)/Zn, S = Zn$^{2+}$ (0.001 M)/Zn. E$^\circ$Zn/Zn$^{2+}$ = − 0.76 V. Electrode potentials of the above electrodes in volts are in the order
questions.explanation: By Nernst equation, E = E° + (0.0592/2)log[Zn$^{2+}$], so electrode potential increases with concentration: Q(0.1M) > R(0.01M) > S(0.001M) > P(0.0001M).

questions.q: The number of angular and radial nodes in 3p orbital respectively are
questions.explanation: Angular nodes = l = 1 for a p orbital; radial nodes = n − l − 1 = 3 − 1 − 1 = 1.

questions.q: The resistance of 0.01 m KCl solution at 298 K is 1500 Ω. If the conductivity of 0.01 m KCl solution at 298 K is 0.146 × 10$^{-3}$ S cm$^{-1}$. The cell constant of the conductivity cell in cm$^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: Cell constant = conductivity × resistance = 0.146×10$^{-3}$ × 1500 = 0.219 cm$^{-1}$.

questions.q: H$_{2(g)}$ + 2AgCl$_{(s)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2 Ag$_{(s)}$ + 2HCl$_{(aq)}$. E$^\circ_{cell}$ at 25°C for the cell is 0.22 V. The equilibrium constant at 25°C is

For a reaction A + 2B → Products, when concentration of B alone is increased half life remains the same. If concentration of A alone is doubled, rate remains the same. The unit of rate constant for the reaction is
questions.explanation: Half-life independent of concentration of B means order in B is 1; rate unchanged when [A] is doubled means order in A is 0. Overall order = 1, so rate constant unit is s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The third ionisation enthalpy is highest in
questions.explanation: Alkaline earth metals have a stable +2 (noble gas-like) configuration; removing a third electron from this stable ion requires very high energy.

questions.q: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by
The rate of a gaseous reaction is given by the expression k[A][B]$^2$. If the volume of vessel is reduced to one half of the initial volume, the reaction rate as compared to original rate is
questions.explanation: Halving volume doubles all concentrations. New rate = k(2A)(2B)$^2$ = 8 × (original rate).

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of [ring with F, NO$_2$ and CH$_2$CH$_3$ (ethyl) substituents — F at C1, NO$_2$ at C2, ethyl at C4] is
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Numbering the ring to give the lowest set of locants to the substituents (alphabetical citation: ethyl, fluoro, nitro) gives 4-Ethyl-1-Fluoro-2-nitrobenzene.

questions.q: Higher order ( > 3) reactions are rare due to
options: Shifting of equilibrium towards reactants due to elastic collisions
Loss of active species on collision
Low probability of simultaneous collision of all reacting species
Increase in entropy as more molecules are involved
questions.explanation: The probability that more than three molecules collide simultaneously with correct orientation and energy is extremely low, making higher order reactions rare.

questions.q: Arrange benzene, n-hexane and ethyne in decreasing order of their acidic behaviour
questions.explanation: Acidity of C–H bond increases with s-character: sp (ethyne) > sp$^2$ (benzene) > sp$^3$ (n-hexane), giving ethyne > Benzene > n-hexane.

questions.q: A colloidal solution is subjected to an electric field than colloidal particles more towards anode. The amount of electrolytes of BaCl$_2$, AlCl$_3$ and NaCl required to coagulate the given colloid is in the order
questions.explanation: The colloid is negatively charged, so cations coagulate it; by the Hardy–Schulze rule, coagulating power increases with cationic charge (Al$^{3+}$>Ba$^{2+}$>Na$^+$), so the amount required decreases in the same order: NaCl > BaCl$_2$ > AlCl$_3$.

questions.q: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: Hydrogen bonding is stronger than dispersion forces
Sigma bonds are stronger than π-bonds
σ-electrons are referred to as mobile electrons
questions.explanation: It is the delocalised π-electrons (e.g. in aromatic/conjugated systems), not σ-electrons, that are referred to as mobile electrons; hence statement (D) is incorrect.

questions.q: Zeta potential is
options: Potential required to bring about coagulation of a colloidal sol.
Potential required to give the particle a speed of 1 cm S$^{-1}$
Potential difference between fixed charged layer and the diffused layer having opposite charges
Potential energy of the colloidal particles.
questions.explanation: Zeta (electrokinetic) potential is defined as the potential difference between the fixed (compact) layer and the diffuse layer of opposite charge surrounding a colloidal particle.

questions.q: Which of the following compound on heating gives N$_2$O?
questions.explanation: On heating, NH$_4$NO$_3$ decomposes to give N$_2$O and water; Pb(NO$_3$)$_2$ gives NO$_2$+O$_2$, NH$_4$NO$_2$ gives N$_2$, and NaNO$_3$ gives NaNO$_2$+O$_2$.

questions.q: Which of the following property is true for the given sequence NH$_3$ > PH$_3$ > AsH$_3$ > SbH$_3$ > BiH$_3$?
questions.explanation: Both thermal stability and bond angle decrease in this order down group 15 hydrides (KEA accepted both B and C as correct).

questions.q: The correct order of boiling point in the following compounds is
questions.explanation: Boiling points: H$_2$O (100°C) > HF (19.5°C) > NH$_3$ (−33°C), due to the extent of hydrogen bonding and molecular association.

questions.q: XeF$_6$ on partial hydrolysis gives a compound X, which has square pyramidal geometry. 'X' is
questions.explanation: Partial hydrolysis of XeF$_6$ gives XeOF$_4$, which has a square pyramidal shape (AX$_5$E).

questions.q: A colourless, neutral, paramagnetic oxide of Nitrogen 'P' on oxidation gives reddish brown gas Q. Q on cooling gives colourless gas R. R on reaction with P gives blue solid S. Identify P, Q, R, S, respectively
questions.explanation: NO (P, colourless paramagnetic) oxidises to NO$_2$ (Q, reddish brown), which dimerises on cooling to N$_2$O$_4$ (R, colourless); NO + NO$_2$ gives blue N$_2$O$_3$ (S).

questions.q: Which of the following does not represent property stated against it?
options: Ti < V < Mn – Number of oxidation states
questions.explanation: Density actually increases across the 3d series from Sc to Fe (Sc lowest, Fe higher) due to increasing atomic mass with roughly similar atomic size, so 'Sc > Cr > Fe' is incorrect.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct for all elements from Sc to Cu?
options: The lowest oxidation state shown by them is +2
4S orbital is completely filled in the ground state
3d orbital is not completely filled in the ground state
The ions in +2 oxidation states are paramagnetic
questions.explanation: From Sc$^{2+}$(d$^1$) to Cu$^{2+}$(d$^9$), every M$^{2+}$ ion in this series has at least one unpaired electron, so all are paramagnetic; the other statements have exceptions (e.g. Cr, Cu for 4s; Cu for 3d).

questions.q: When the absolute temperature of ideal gas is doubled and pressure is halved, the volume of gas
options: will be half of original volume
will be 4 times the original volume
will be 2 times the original volume
will be 1/4th times the original volume
questions.explanation: From PV = nRT, V$_2$ = nR(2T)/(P/2) = 4 × (nRT/P) = 4V$_1$.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs has both the ions coloured in aqueous solution? [Atomic numbers of Sc = 21, Ti = 22, Ni = 28, Cu = 29, Mn = 25]
questions.explanation: Sc$^{3+}$(d$^0$), Ti$^{4+}$(d$^0$) and Cu$^+$(d$^{10}$) are colourless; Mn$^{2+}$(d$^5$) and Ti$^{3+}$(d$^1$) both have unpaired d-electrons and are coloured.

questions.q: For the crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes,
options: the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will decrease by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will increase by (2/5)Δ$_0$
the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will increase by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will decrease by (2/5)Δ$_0$
the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will increase by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will increase by (2/5)Δ$_0$
the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will decrease by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will decrease by (2/5)Δ$_0$
questions.explanation: In octahedral crystal field splitting, e$_g$ orbitals are raised by (3/5)Δ$_0$ while t$_{2g}$ orbitals are lowered by (2/5)Δ$_0$ relative to the barycentre.

questions.q: Peroxide effect is observed with the addition of HBr but not with the addition of HI to unsymmetrical alkene because
options: H-I bond is stronger that H-Br and is not cleaved by the free radical
H-I bond is weaker than H-Br bond so that iodine free radicals combine to form iodine molecules
Bond strength of HI and HBr are same but free radicals are formed in HBr
questions.explanation: Since the H–I bond is weaker, iodine free radicals formed recombine to give I$_2$ (an exothermic, favourable process) instead of continuing the radical chain, so the peroxide effect is not observed with HI.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$(CO$_3$)] Cl is
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before carbonato) as prefixes to the metal name, giving Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) Chloride; since the complex ion is a cation, no '-ate' suffix is used.

questions.q: Homoleptic complexes among the following are: (A) K$_3$[Al(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$], (B) [CoCl(en)$_2$]$^+$ (C) K$_2$[Zn(OH)$_4$]
questions.explanation: Homoleptic complexes have only one kind of ligand: K$_3$[Al(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$] (only oxalate) and K$_2$[Zn(OH)$_4$] (only hydroxide) are homoleptic; [CoCl(en)$_2$]$^+$ has two different ligands (heteroleptic).

questions.q: The correct order for wavelengths of light absorbed in the complex ions [CoCl(NH$_3$)$_5$]$^{2+}$, [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ and [Co(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$ is
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series Cl$^-$ < NH$_3$ < CN$^-$, crystal field splitting Δ$_0$ increases in that order, and wavelength absorbed is inversely related to Δ$_0$, giving [CoCl(NH$_3$)$_5$]$^{2+}$ > [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ > [Co(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$.

questions.q: [2-ethyl-1-nitrobenzene ring] $\xrightarrow{Br_2, UV\ light}$ A. The compound A (major product) is [benzylic bromination at the ethyl CH$_2$ group]
options: 3-Bromo-4-ethyl-1-nitrobenzene (Br on ring, ortho to the ethyl group)
questions.explanation: Br$_2$/UV light causes free-radical substitution at the more stable benzylic position, replacing an H on the CH$_2$ adjacent to the ring to give the benzylic bromide, CH(Br)CH$_3$.

questions.q: Bond enthalpies of A$_2$, B$_2$ and AB are in the ratio 2 : 1 : 2. If bond enthalpy of formation of AB is −100 KJ mol$^{-1}$. The bond enthalpy of B$_2$ is
The order of reactivity of the compounds C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Br, C$_6$H$_5$CH(C$_6$H$_5$)Br, C$_6$H$_5$CH(CH$_3$)Br and C$_6$H$_5$C(CH$_3$)(C$_6$H$_5$)Br in S$_N$2 reaction is
questions.explanation: S$_N$2 rate decreases as steric bulk around the reacting carbon increases, so the least hindered primary benzylic bromide (C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Br) reacts fastest and the most substituted one reacts slowest.

questions.q: The major product of the following reaction is CH$_2$ = CH – CH$_2$ – OH $\xrightarrow[Excess]{HBr}$ product
questions.explanation: Excess HBr first substitutes the allylic OH to give allyl bromide, then adds across the double bond (Markovnikov) to give CH$_3$–CHBr–CH$_2$Br.

questions.q: [Cumene] + O$_2$ $\rightarrow$ [cumene hydroperoxide] $\xrightarrow[H_2O]{H^+}$ A+B. The product 'A' gives white precipitate when treated with bromine water. The product 'B' is treated with Barium hydroxide to give the product C. The compound C is heated strongly to form product D. The product D is
questions.explanation: Cumene process gives phenol (A, gives white ppt with bromine water) and acetone (B); base-catalysed aldol condensation of acetone gives diacetone alcohol (C), which on strong heating dehydrates to mesityl oxide, 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (D).

questions.q: For the reaction A(g) + B (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ C(g) + D(g); ΔH = − QKJ. The equilibrium constant cannot be disturbed by
questions.explanation: Since Δn$_{gas}$ = 0 for this reaction, changing pressure has no effect on the equilibrium constant (or even the equilibrium position); only temperature change alters K.

questions.q: An organic compound 'X' on treatment with PCC in dichloromethane gives the compound Y. Compound 'Y' reacts with I$_2$ and alkali to form yellow precipitate of triiodomethane. The compound X is
questions.explanation: PCC oxidises a primary alcohol only to an aldehyde. Since Y gives a positive iodoform test, Y is CH$_3$CHO, so X is ethanol (CH$_3$CH$_2$OH).

questions.q: A compound 'A' (C$_7$H$_8$O) is insoluble in NaHCO$_3$ solution but dissolve in NaOH and gives a characteristic colour with neutral FeCl$_3$ solution. When treated with Bromine water compound 'A' forms the compound B with the formula C$_7$H$_5$OBr$_3$. 'A' is
options: Benzyl alcohol: ring with a CH$_2$OH substituent (not phenolic)
m-Cresol: ring with OH and CH$_3$ on carbons separated by one position (meta)
o-Cresol: ring with OH and CH$_3$ on adjacent carbons (ortho)
p-Cresol: ring with OH and CH$_3$ on opposite carbons (para)
questions.explanation: A is soluble in NaOH (phenolic, not carboxylic since insoluble in NaHCO$_3$) and gives colour with FeCl$_3$, so it is a cresol (methylphenol). Only m-cresol leaves all three ring positions activated by -OH (2,4,6) free of the methyl group, so it can brominate at all three to give the tribromo derivative C$_7$H$_5$OBr$_3$; in o- and p-cresol the methyl group occupies one of these activated positions, allowing only a dibromo product.

questions.q: In set of reactions, identify D: CH$_3$COOH $\xrightarrow{SOCl_2}$ A $\xrightarrow[Anh\ AlCl_3]{Benzene}$ B $\xrightarrow{HCN}$ C $\xrightarrow{H_2O}$ D
questions.explanation: A is CH$_3$COCl, B is acetophenone (from Friedel–Crafts acylation), C is the cyanohydrin of acetophenone, and D is its hydrolysis product, the α-hydroxy carboxylic acid (2-phenyl-2-hydroxypropanoic acid analogue).

questions.q: K$_a$ values for acids H$_2$SO$_3$, HNO$_2$, CH$_3$COOH and HCN are respectively 1.3 × 10$^{-2}$, 4 ×10$^{-4}$, 1.8 × 10$^{-5}$ and 4 × 10$^{-10}$, which of the above acids produces stronger conjugate base in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: The weakest acid produces the strongest conjugate base. HCN has the smallest K$_a$, so it is the weakest acid and gives the strongest conjugate base (CN$^-$).

questions.q: A $\xrightarrow[H_2O]{Hg SO_4/H_2SO_4}$, B $\xrightarrow{PCC}$, C $\xrightarrow[(ii) H_3O^+]{(i) SnCl_2/HCl}$ → Acetaldehyde. A, B and C respectively are
questions.explanation: Ethyne on Hg$^{2+}$/H$_2$SO$_4$ catalysed hydration gives acetaldehyde (A); PCC oxidises ethanol to acetaldehyde (B); Stephen reduction (SnCl$_2$/HCl then H$_3$O$^+$) converts ethanenitrile to acetaldehyde (C).

questions.q: The reagent which can do the conversion CH$_3$COOH → CH$_3$ – CH$_2$ – OH is
questions.explanation: LiAlH$_4$ is a strong reducing agent capable of reducing carboxylic acids directly to primary alcohols; NaBH$_4$ cannot reduce carboxylic acids.

questions.q: CH$_3$CHO $\xrightarrow[(ii) H_3O^+]{(i) CH_3MgBr}$ A $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{Conc\ H_2SO_4}$ B $\xrightarrow[(ii) H_2O, OH^-]{(i) B_2H_6}$ C. A and C are
questions.explanation: A is isopropanol (2-propanol) from Grignard addition; dehydration gives propene (B); hydroboration–oxidation of propene (anti-Markovnikov) gives 1-propanol (C). A and C are both C$_3$H$_8$O but differ in OH position, so they are position isomers.

questions.q: Which of the following is not true for oxidation?
questions.explanation: Removal of an electronegative element is characteristic of reduction, not oxidation.

questions.q: Which is the most suitable reagent for the following conversion? CH$_3$ – CH = CH – CH$_2$ – C(=O) – CH$_3$ $\rightarrow$ CH$_3$ – CH = CH – CH$_2$ – C(=O) –OH
options: I$_2$ and NaOH solution with subsequent acidification
questions.explanation: The haloform reaction (I$_2$/NaOH followed by acidification) selectively cleaves a methyl ketone to a carboxylic acid (losing one carbon as CHI$_3$) without affecting the C=C double bond.

questions.q: C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Cl $\xrightarrow{alc.\ NH_3}$ A $\xrightarrow{2CH_3Cl}$ B. The product B is
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride with ammonia gives benzylamine (A, phenylmethanamine), which on further methylation with 2 mol CH$_3$Cl gives N,N-dimethyl phenylmethanamine (B).

questions.q: The method by which aniline cannot be prepared is
options: Nitration of benzene followed by reduction with Sn and con HCl
Degradation of benzamide with bromine in alkaline solution
Reduction of nitrobenzene with H$_2$ / Pd is ethanol
Potassium salt of phthalimide treated with chlorobenzene followed by the hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH solution
questions.explanation: Gabriel synthesis requires an alkyl halide; chlorobenzene (aryl halide) does not undergo the required nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion, so aniline cannot be prepared this way.

questions.q: Permanent hardness cannot be removed by
questions.explanation: Clark's method (addition of lime) removes only temporary (bicarbonate) hardness by precipitating carbonate; it is not effective for permanent (chloride/sulphate) hardness.

questions.q: A hydrocarbon A (C$_4$H$_8$) on reaction with HCl gives a compound B (C$_4$H$_9$Cl) which on reaction with 1 mol of NH$_3$ gives compound C (C$_4$H$_{10}$N). On reacting with NaNO$_2$ and HCl followed by treatment with water, compound C yields an optically active compound D. The D is
questions.explanation: A is but-2-ene, B is 2-chlorobutane, C is sec-butylamine (2-aminobutane, chiral). Diazotization (NaNO$_2$/HCl) of the primary amine followed by hydrolysis with water replaces NH$_2$ with OH to give the optically active 2-butanol.

questions.q: RNA and DNA are chiral molecules, their chirality is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: The D-configured sugars (ribose in RNA, deoxyribose in DNA) are chiral and are responsible for the overall chirality of the nucleic acid chains.

questions.q: The property of the alkaline earth metals that increases with their atomic number is
options: Solubility of their hydroxide in water
Solubility of their sulphate in water
questions.explanation: Down the alkaline earth metal group, hydroxide solubility increases (Be(OH)$_2$ least soluble to Ba(OH)$_2$ most soluble), while ionisation enthalpy, electronegativity and sulphate solubility all decrease.

questions.q: Primary structure in a nucleic acid chain contains bases as G A T G C ........ The chain which is complementary to this chain is
questions.explanation: By complementary base pairing (G pairs with C, A pairs with T), the sequence G-A-T-G-C pairs with C-T-A-C-G.

questions.q: In the detection of II group acid radical, the salt containing chloride is treated with concentrated sulphuric acid, the colourless gas is liberated. The name of the gas is
questions.explanation: Chloride salts react with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ to liberate colourless hydrogen chloride gas.

questions.q: The number of six membered and five membered rings in Buckminster Fullerene respectively is
questions.explanation: Buckminsterfullerene (C$_{60}$) is a truncated icosahedron with 20 six-membered rings and 12 five-membered rings.
